subtasks: S1 action-protocol: ActionCapability.PUBLISH + publish payload + key-level three-state serializer + not-wired 501
S2 policy-engine: deterministic fail-closed verdict between plan_action and resolve_action
S3 action-executor: PUBLISH via Tool Gateway, idempotency key wired, RetryPolicy unlocked

S4a action-mainline-gateway: run_publish submits through the Tool Gateway (no more self-built XHSClient); xhs.publish orphan disappears; cdp_endpoint joins the tool signature so per-account profiles survive the migration; account_id finally reaches the platform layer on the mainline path (closing the other half of the S2 defect)

S4b mainline-confirm: WorkflowStatus.AWAITING_PUBLISH + machine.py branch + interrupt/Command(resume=...); PublisherAgent emits a PublishIntent and stops there; decides open question 1 (ActionIntentRequest.account_id required vs the mainline's implicit account)
notes: S4a landed on feat/p2a-s4a-mainline-gateway (base 5a76cd8a). Scope: only the SUBMIT moved. run_publish no longer builds an XHSClient; it makes one `runtime.tools.invoke("xhs.publish", payload, thread_id=...)` call via BaseAgent.tools (shared_gateway). Ordering is deliberately untouched -- no PublishIntent, no confirmation wait -- because S4 was split: 'reach the Gateway' and 'wait for a human' are orthogonal, and merging them makes the 'migration does not change the contract' red line impossible to verify in isolation. S4b takes the wait. THREE pre-existing facts had to be handled first, found by recon: (1) the mainline never passed account_id at all -- the S2 defect ('account-keyed cooldown has no production writer') had TWO paths from the same XHSPublisher.publish_note, S3 closed the control-plane one, this closes the mainline one; (2) the tool hardcoded settings.platform.cdp_endpoint while the mainline resolves per account, so a straight migration would have silently sent every multi-account publish to the global browser profile -- cdp_endpoint is now a tool parameter (explicit wins, empty falls back to global so the control plane is unchanged); (3) BaseAgent.tools is a property returning shared_gateway(), which PublisherAgent previously bypassed entirely. KEY DESIGN: _publish_gateway_account_id is NOT _publish_account_id. The former returns "" when unspecified, the latter falls back to "default". The idempotency RECORD keeps "default" (compute_publish_id needs a stable string to hash; changing it would re-key every existing record and silently disarm the duplicate guard) while the PLATFORM layer gets "" (handing it "default" would file unattributed posts under account:default and change the meaning of a guardrail that works today). Two call sites, two requirements, two functions. _result_from_gateway is the single place Gateway vocabulary (ok/error_kind) is translated back into the publish_result contract (status/error), which is what keeps the 8 downstream consumers byte-unchanged (analyst/calibrator/analytics/free/workflow/hydration/omp_bridge). Two contract translations were ACCEPTED rather than patched: the timeout wording now belongs to the runtime ("timeout after 900s" replaces the method-name-carrying exception text; the test asserts the VERDICT -- status unknown + error_type publish_result_unknown -- not the wording), and the "RuntimeError: cookie expired..." prefix is harmless because classify_publish_error is a substring match, so auth_expired is unchanged. THE PINNED TRIPWIRE FIRED AND WAS RETARGETED, NOT DELETED: test_audit's 'the only orphan is the publisher' said in its own docstring that P2a wiring a publisher would fail it on purpose; it now asserts orphans == () as test_no_capability_is_left_without_an_agent, and the four-tool-users list became five. MOOT POINT WORTH RECORDING: the mutation 'the tool ignores the cdp_endpoint it is handed' SURVIVED on the first full run. Asking 'is the mutated code actually executed?' showed it is NOT -- every test replaces _get_publisher wholesale, so the factory body (and the explicit-beats-global rule) had ZERO execution coverage. A real gap, not a fake mutation: TestGetPublisherEndpointSelection now patches only XHSPublisher so the selection logic really runs, and the mutant dies. Gates: pytest 3151 passed/3 skipped (3144 + 7 = exactly the new cases: test_run_publish +4, test_xhs_publisher +3 -> zero existing cases changed apart from the intended tripwire), ruff 499 files, mypy 202 files clean, P1b baseline drift within threshold, tool_runtime_gate OK with publisher.py declared=1 invoked=1 and the orphan line GONE (named by agents: 10, orphans == ()). Mutation self-check 13/13 killed, each from original bytes by a named assertion; M1/M2/M12 (declaration/call-site capability names) are killed by the GATE first, which is the point of a compile-time rule. Stub seam: patch backend.tools.xhs.publisher._get_publisher -- browser layer only -- so the tool's normalisation, the catalog and the Gateway all really run; file runtime dropped 125.8s -> 4.3s, i.e. those tests used to touch a real browser. Open question 3 is now half-answered in code: the mainline passes its content-level publish_id AS the runtime's request-level idempotency_key (documented in-place, still no formal verdict). Open question 1 and the 501 fallback remain S4b/S5's.
